items.title: FemShep 配音演员詹妮弗·黑尔在《质量效应 5》预告片在线曝光后发声
items.summary: Award-winning voice actor Jennifer Hale, best known for voicing the female version of Commander Shepard in the

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/22/me-1792674182792.jpg

Award-winning voice actor Jennifer Hale, best known for voicing the female version of Commander Shepard in the first three Mass Effect games, is speaking out after a leaked trailer for the sci-fi franchise’s next title was leaked online.

The Mass Effect community was hit hard this week by news that EA is closing down BioWare , the 30-year-old studio known for spearheading Western RPGs with series like Dragon Age, Mass Effect, Jade Empire, and others.

Rubbing salt in the wound, EA also revealed the next Mass Effect game (supposedly titled Mass Effect Universe) was canceled. This revelation hurt even more after staff who formerly worked on the project spoke out about it online , with one even leaking a full-length trailer for the game on Reddit. This trailer promised a game that would have been everything fans wanted and more — and it even caught the attention of FemShep herself.
Hale responded to a re-upload of the Mass Effect 5 trailer on X/Twitter, and it seems she’s just as hopeful as the rest of us that somehow, some way, the game will still get made.
“It's extraordinary,” she wrote . “I’m holding hope for magic to happen. This community and you incredible devs deserve that and more.”

Two days prior, she went live on Instagram alongside fellow Commander Shepard voice actor Mark Meer, who plays the male version of the character, to address fans in the wake of EA’s devastating decision

“I feel weirdly hopeful, and I can’t explain why,” Hale said. “...I feel for the [BioWare] employees who are suddenly unemployed. That is the number one thing on my mind. Those beautiful team members who are looking for a new home.”

“It is very sad news,” Meer added. “It is a massive loss for Edmonton, for Canada, and for the video game industry in general. It’s very unfortunate to see. And of course, I feel very bad for all of the fans.”

“It’s really hard to think about BioWare being shut down, but it was in the hands of ownership that may not have understood what BioWare fully is,” Hale continued. “And I’m hopeful that maybe, there might be some crazy thing where they decide that. in order to increase their profit margins — which is often their priority — they will release these IPs into the market to sell them, and use that to do what they do, which is increase their profit margins. But maybe, someone could grab hold of these IPs and do something with them.”

Hale isn’t alone in this line of thinking; many fans are calling on EA to at least sell BioWare’s intellectual properties to other developers in the hopes that Mass Effect 5 can eventually be released. Even Canadian politicians are getting in on the conversation, with the country’s New Democratic Party leader Avi Lewis taking to social media to publicly call out EA.

However, industry insiders and analysts are urging caution around this particular idea. Speaking with IGN, three separate analysts stated that BioWare’s library of titles simply don’t align with EA’s current strategy, and said it’s unlikely the company relinquishes them to other companies. What’s more, these IPs are likely to be extremely expensive, to the point where other studios simply wouldn’t have the funds nor the time to pursue them.

Former BioWare executive producer Mark Darrah shared a similar sentiment , though he admitted that, given EA is now looking to cut costs to cover its massive debt, it might consider the idea of selling these IPs off — but said it’s just as likely that execs “just try to forget that they ever existed and bury them in the vault.”

items.summary: The Magic: The Gathering The Hobbit Gift Bundle is on sale at Amazon, but here is why crunching the numbers pr

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/09/17/header-1788811440204-1789661524667.jpg

Magic: The Gathering’s crossovers tend to draw a mixed response from the hardcore fans who want more of Jace, Liliana, and Gideon over the Avengers, but if there’s one crossover that’s been universally praised, it was Lord of the Rings.

Wizards of the Coast looked to follow suit this year with a return to Middle-Earth, and while The Hobbit offers a smaller set than the 2023 original, it’s still packed with great cards. And while this new Amazon deal might be tempting, here’s why we think you’re better off holding your nerve for a few weeks.
This Hobbit x Magic Deal Is Likely To Get Better
Amazon’s latest offering has the Magic x The Hobbit Gift Bundle down from $109.86 to $99.99, a 9% discount .

It’s not the steepest cut we’ve seen, but it does look like a new low price. Inside, you’ll find nine Play Boosters worth $6.99 each, as well as 34 land cards that include full-art seasonal hobbit lands in surge foil and full-art Middle-Earth Journey lands. There’s also an alternate-art promo card, but the real draw is likely to be the Collector Booster.

These can often be priced even higher than the $38 or so you’ll find them for in your local game store, and are the place you’re most likely to unwrap one of the rarest cards in the set , like Gleaming Splendor, The Arkenstone, or Smaug.
When you crunch the numbers, you’re not actually saving any more than a couple of bucks on this bundle than buying its separate parts (I’m not factoring in the lands and storage box, admittedly).

With that in mind, this one feels ripe for a discount closer to the sales season. In recent years, we’ve seen Magic sets drop in price, even those launching in the same year. Expect the same to happen here.

items.summary: Prolific and veteran gaming actor Jennifer Hale, who is known for voicing Commander Shepard in the Mass Effect

others.title: 泄露的《质量效应 5》预告片是真实的，让我们一睹被取消的游戏的风采

content.v: Prolific and veteran gaming actor Jennifer Hale, who is known for voicing Commander Shepard in the Mass Effect series, has reacted to the closure of BioWare and the cancellation of the next game in the series. After footage of the new project, Mass Effect Universe , was released, Hale said , "It's extraordinary."
She added: "I’m holding hope for magic to happen. This community and you incredible vevs deserve that and more."

A "Save Mass Effect" Change.org petition was launched this week to urge EA to "take decisive action by committing to the continued development of Mass Effect." The petition has more than 65,000 signatures so far.

All of BioWare's new releases in the past decade--Mass Effect: Andromeda, Anthem, and Dragon Age: The Veilguard--were commercial disappointments. Against that backdrop, closing the studio makes a lot of financial sense , but it's upsetting to the millions of Mass Effect fans who adore the franchise and want to see it continue.
Based on insider reporting, the new Mass Effect game would have mixed covert ops with John Wick-inspired action , and that got a lot of people excited about what could have been.

Composer Bear McCreary, who has done work for the God of War and Call of Duty franchises, reacted to BioWare's closure, too . Asked if the laid-off BioWare developers could take what they had and complete the project as a "spiritual successor" via crowdfunding, McCreary said it's a good idea but is probably unrealistic.
"Man, I want to believe. But, I just gotta ask... How many examples are there of this really working in the past? And of those examples, how many were a project as big as Mass Effect?" he said.
Avi Lewis, a Canadian politician, has called on the government to help save BioWare by providing “federal support” to the workers to buy it back.

“This is private equity, this is what it does,” he said. “Buy up businesses, run them into the ground, and rip them apart for short-term profit. The developers at BioWare know how to run the studio. They know how to make the games we all love. They should be given the first opportunity–and the federal support–to buy it and run it themselves.”
The new Mass Effect game was revealed in 2020 . Since then, the game remained in “early development” until its cancellation this week.
While the new Mass Effect game is not going ahead, the Mass Effect TV show for Prime Video remains in development .

The closure of BioWare and cancellation of the new Mass Effect game came as part of a wider shakeup at EA following its sale to an investor consortium including Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners. EA cut jobs, canceled games, and scaled back in other ways as part of the shakeup, as the publisher faces a huge debt repayment schedule.

items.title: 《质量效应 5》取消后细节揭晓，包括任务中的“杀手式自由”
items.summary: Following the cancellation of Mass Effect 5, purportedly called Mass Effect Universe, last week – alongside th

content.v: Following this week's cancellation of Mass Effect 5, purportedly called Mass Effect Universe – alongside the closure of the entire BioWare development studio – new gameplay details about the role-playing game revival have emerged, including handcrafted missions that gave players Hitman-style freedom, the abililty to hack the environment, brutal close-range executions, the return of Liara, and much more.

YouTube content creator Dantics revealed the details in a new video , as he was a member of the Mass Effect Council – a group of external Mass Effect community members who gave BioWare feedback on the game during development. IGN has verified the legitimacy of these details, and can add that a development source told us that BioWare had "every major [alien] race" working in the build.

Dantics says it "looked incredible" and added , "From what I saw, BioWare was making Mass Effect for us, the fans." More specifically, he shared that the new Mass Effect was set over 600 years after the Reaper War, and your customizable agent was like a John Wick/James Bond-type character who has had experimental technology implanted in you. As a result, you'd be able to hack and manipulate the environment such as letting you "see through walls, identify systems, remotely trigger hazards, and more." Furthermore, you'd also be able to perform "brutal, close-range executions."

Meanwhile, the galaxy has been divided into three major factions, with humanity, the Krogans, the Batarians, and others allied together. The Council races formed their own alliance, while the Geth had emerged as a third superpower who constructed megastructures. Dantics describes the setting of Mass Effect Universe as "a galactic Cold War instead of another Reaper-style invasion with a shadowy adversary."

Missions would've been handcrafted, like in the original trilogy, "but with Hitman-style freedom in how you complete them." Your squadmates would be able to clash with each other, while romance options would return without being "sanitized." Finally, Liara would return from the original trilogy, now as a powerful Asari Matriarch.

BioWare's closure and Mass Effect 5's cancellation have saddened many in the gaming community. I wrote a eulogy about how BioWare was the greatest RPG developer ever . Our own Jackie Thomas lamented that we'll never get to see the series redeemed after the disappointment of Mass Effect Andromeda, and IGN's Matt Purslow believed that EA never knew what it had with BioWare . An internal trailer leaked online following the cancellation that gives us all an idea of what BioWare was building.

Fans aren't giving up yet, though, as an online petition has already surged past 50,000 signatures. In addition, a Canadian politician is calling on the government to support BioWare developers in a buyout that would enable to run the studio independently. We spoke to a number of analysts this week to find out why EA shut BioWare down, and the chances of a franchise selloff .

items.title: 下一个质量效应听起来就像太空中的约翰威克
items.summary: After news broke that EA would be shutting down BioWare , more details on the studio's in-development Mass Eff

content.v: After news broke that EA would be shutting down BioWare , more details on the studio's in-development Mass Effect have begun to trickle out. A trailer for Mass Effect Universe hinted that the next game in the series would have a completely different tone, moving away from the galactic warfare that defined the first three games and toward covert ops, espionage, and the occasional barroom shootout. Gaming content creator and YouTuber Dantics has shed more light on the game, describing it as a Mass Effect game for the fans.

Known for his lore videos, including several on Mass Effect, Dantics says he was part of a private "Mass Effect Council," a community feedback group of content creators who helped advise BioWare's small team.

Dantics says that Mass Effect Universe was set over 600 years after the Reaper War, and players would step into the boots of a customizable N7 agent. Players would also have a much smaller arsenal of weapons that would make them feel like a "cross between John Wick and James Bond," and they'd be working to take down a sinister force that was operating in the shadows of a galactic cold war. While Commander Shepard was a soldier, your N7 character was going to be an "agent" who would rely on cunning to get through encounters, but could apply pressure when needed--ballistic pressure, that is.

Following the destruction of the relays at the end of the Reaper War, the fast-travel hubs had been rebuilt, and technology had advanced at a rapid pace. Shepard's legacy had been preserved centuries after their death; three new powerful alliances had arisen: Council races had formed their own faction, while humanity had aligned itself with Krogans, Batarians, and other superpowers. The Geth--a synthetic, network-based artificial intelligence species--had become a third power, and Dantics said there would be connections between the Milky Way and Andromeda galaxies, thanks to the Geth building superstructure relays.

So what would the gameplay have been like? Dantics says that your N7 agent would be implanted with experimental technology to give them an edge in battle, allowing you to hack and manipulate the environment to your advantage, similar to hacking in Cyberpunk 2077. Missions would have a handcrafted feel to them, but with "Hitman-style freedom" in how you complete them. Squadmates would also feature in the game, and this time, they could clash with each other. Dantics also mentioned that romance "wasn't being sanitized," something the leaked Mass Effect trailer alluded to with some saucy scenes. A familiar face from the past would also return, as Liara T'Soni was still alive and had grown into a powerful Asari Matriarch.

Mass Effect universe has been shelved, but it has been reported that the TV show based on the sci-fi series is still in development . Experts have also spoken about EA's decision, saying that it sadly does make business sense , while Former BioWare executive producer Mark Darrah has suggested that EA could sell the Mass Effect IP in the future. It might have been bad timing, but this week also saw Archetype Entertainment release a new trailer for its Mass Effect spiritual successor , Exodus.

items.title: BioWare 可能已经消失，但它的精神在这些游戏中继续存在
items.summary: BioWare was shut down by EA earlier this week. While the studio had struggled through a long stretch without p

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/23/bioware-lives-on-blogroll-1792774338672.jpg

BioWare was shut down by EA earlier this week . While the studio had struggled through a long stretch without putting out a genuine classic, it’s no lie to say it was behind some of the best RPGs of all time . At its peak, with games like Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic , Mass Effect and Dragon Age: Origins , BioWare was a pioneer of not only building worlds, but filling those worlds with characters I (and so many others) actually cared about.

But BioWare went so much further than just writing some witty dialog and calling it a day. I always think back to the Mass Effect 2’s climactic suicide mission, where, unless you’ve completed all of your companions’ loyalty quests and built up those relationships, there was a real chance they would just die, never to return in the trilogy’s final chapter. BioWare built personal, heartbreaking consequences into its stories.

The games BioWare made in its heyday were incredibly influential, but I don’t think there are any games from other developers that tried to build on those successes that truly hit the same level. Even BioWare struggled to capture that same magic in its latter games. But while I don’t think there is anything out there close to the ultimate quality of the Mass Effect trilogy or the first three Dragon Age games, the spirit of BioWare’s best work does live on in the work of the games they inspired.

Just in the last few years, there have been plenty of games that draw straight from BioWare’s well, and there are quite a few projects in the works, including two that look like they could just be new BioWare games. So if you’re hunting for more BioWare in the wake of this terrible news, here are six games to keep in mind.
Baldur’s Gate 3

Now, obviously BioWare made the first two Baldur’s Gate games, so of course they had a massive influence on the third one. But each time I go back to Larian’s Baldur’s Gate 3 , the influence from Mass Effect and Dragon Age becomes more obvious. The way it introduces your companions and encourages you to build close relationships, for example, is extremely BioWare.

That’s not to mention the complicated web of different romance options in the game. I ended up wooing Lae’Zel, and spent hours building her into a reliable tank to carry me through the late game. And then I made a really bad decision involving a mind flayer, and she just straight up left my party for good. I had to figure out how to adjust my party (and my broken heart) from there.

Earlier in that playthrough, I ended up accidentally killing a potential companion, just because of some choices I made when trying to help some fellow paladins in Act One. It wasn’t until my next playthrough that I even realized they were someone I could recruit, and when I did realize it, I felt awful. In many ways, this chain of action and consequence mirrors what I love so much about Mass Effect 2’s suicide mission, but in Baldur’s Gate 3, it spans the entire game.

Even outside your little web of companions, the choices you make are core to what makes Baldur’s Gate 3 tick. From the outset, the game throws seriously consequential decisions your way that can come back to bite you in the ass depending on what you choose to do with them. Early on, there’s a commune of druids that are having a spat with some visiting Tieflings, and the way you handle that doesn’t just affect the scenario, but begins a domino effect that extends through the whole campaign. There are some pretty dark ways that situation can play out, too, and that’s just one of the dozens of encounters you have to deal with that shapes your character and playthrough.
The Outer Worlds

Most of the time, The Outer Worlds feels like Fallout: New Vegas in space. That’s a pretty natural conclusion, considering it’s developed by New Vegas studio Obsidian Entertainment. But just like Baldur’s Gate 3, The Outer Worlds frequently feels exactly like a BioWare game, thanks to the way it handles its six companions. No matter how many wild situations the game puts you through, the thing that always sticks with me when I go back to The Outer Worlds is how fleshed out the companions are.

All of them have their own distinct needs, leading to side quest chains that will ultimately decide their fate. And, similar to both Mass Effect and Dragon Age’s decision-tallying finales, there’s an entire tree of different endings that change depending on the choices you make. A lot of the questlines that dictate those endings cross over each other too, creating this tangled web of possibilities that can potentially make every playthrough just a little bit different.
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered

CD Projekt Red and BioWare go way back, with the original Witcher game being built on the same engine as Neverwinter Nights . So, it’s not surprising that The Witcher games have carried the spirit of BioWare’s approach to storytelling for years. And that feels a little weird to say, because when I think of BioWare, I think of RPGs with a protagonist that you create yourself, and companions that surround you for the entire course of the game – two things The Witcher doesn’t have. In all of the Witcher games you play as Geralt of Rivia and, occasionally, other characters from the books, and the allies you gather aren’t party companions in the BioWare sense of the word.

I go back and forth with myself all the time over which of these games I love the most, but The Witcher 3 is probably the best example of CDPR taking BioWare’s legacy and running with it. You spend most of your time in The Witcher 3 on your own, trying to find Geralt’s adoptive daughter, Ciri. But even though you are by yourself most of the time, there’s a huge focus on doing side missions for supporting characters to build up allegiances ahead of when – spoilers – the villainous Wild Hunt attacks your fortress home of Kaer Morhen. Right off the bat, that leaves a lot of potential for an ending reminiscent of Mass Effect 2’s iconic final mission, but unfortunately not a lot happens if you fail to recruit friends to help defend the Witcher fortress.

Still, The Witcher 3 is a game I’ve played through four or five times, and even though I know there’s not much of a gameplay purpose to recruiting everyone, I still try to get all my friends into that castle in the mountains, even if it just means unlocking dialog that makes me feel warm and fuzzy.
Exodus

It’s no secret that for the last decade or so, even before EA shuttered BioWare, things were rough for the studio. A lot of talented people jumped ship, especially in the run-up to Anthem. One of the studios that formed from these talented ex-BioWare folks is Archetype Entertainment, and its first game, Exodus , is due out on April 7 next year.

We’ve actually got the chance to play a bit of Exodus early, and from what I’ve seen and read from my colleagues, it looks as much like a new Mass Effect game as yesterday’s leaked trailer. It’s a squad-based sci-fi RPG, and one of your squadmates is an octopus in a giant mech. That sounds ridiculous, and it is, but just look at the wild and wonderful companions we got in Mass Effect. In the trailer we got at Gamescom, there were scenes that made it look like we’re going to meet their family. So, it at least seems like there’s going to be some suitably wild companion quests in the game.

items.summary: I'm a chump who can't tell my gems from my minerals.

content.v: I have never really thought much about gemstones or minerals, which is weird considering one of my all-time favourite games is Minecraft, in which I spend a bulk of my time strip-mining. But Abyssal Lapidary has made me realise that there is so much more to the dirt than just coal.

In the demo for Abyssal Lapidary I got to begin my stint as a lapidarist, someone who cuts, shapes, grinds, and polishes minerals to make pretty gemstones. The only problem is, like I said before, I don't really know stones.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/wxdirrriCEEotRDdkXz2cJ-1920-80.jpg

Abyssal Lapidary doesn't exactly drop you in the deep end but it does expect you to pick up with the art of making and selling gemstones rather quickly. My first step was searching around the rather large house I'd found myself in which was apparently part of a declining business but it seemed rather nice; it even had a balcony.

Most of the doors downstairs were locked, part of the later progression of the game, the few things I did have access to included a station for fixing tools, breaking rocks, and a booth to talk to customers.

Throughout the day people will turn up to my humble business either looking to buy some precious gemstones or selling minerals and rocks that I can mine into. There's also a guy looking for mysterious artefacts, someone trying to give me a loan (suspicious), and a nice lady selling tea. I'm not 100% sure about what the tea does yet but I buy it anyways.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/i4R3zPVt5om32ZDx6eVpYJ-1920-80.jpg

The rest of my day was spent sitting at my desk carefully hammering rocks into smaller rocks, looking to see if they had anything precious inside. I found some ordinary apatite, fine apatite, and crude duskstone; yeah I'm pretty good at this rock thing.
After selling my wares I managed to earn enough renown to apply for my Silver License which allowed me to access the gem faceting table; this is what I'm here for.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/MEpdeExZcmxYY6CCrvsKJJ-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Bdvn6mJWDF5h2BFku5PiQJ-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/i4R3zPVt5om32ZDx6eVpYJ-1920-80.jpg

Turning regular clumps of gemstones into cut gems not only adds quite a bit of monetary value to them, it's also quite a lot of fun. The faceting table is essentially a metal sanding machine that you press gems into to whittle them into a desired shape like an old single cut, table cut, or point cut; there are likely more but this is all I have access to right now, and as I'll reiterate I don't know jack about gems.

Grinding the gems down can be surprisingly hard as there's only a small window in which you can cut them perfectly, grind them for too long or not long enough and they'll lose a lot of value. And I cannot afford to lose money right now.

Abyssal Lapidary can be quite slow at times, it's helped by the fact that you can fast forward time to stop you from just milling around or staring out the window for six hours. I'm sure there'll be more ways to fill your day as rooms and work benches open up around the store, but I honestly don't mind its methodical, relaxing approach to procuring, mining, and fixing up gemstones. Who knows? Perhaps by the time the full game launches I'll be able to tell a garnet from a chrysoberyl.

items.title: Humble Bundle 的科幻曝光捆绑包包含 8 款游戏，售价 25 美元，其中包括《Marathon》
items.summary: To celebrate its 15th anniversary, Humble Bundle has dropped a new Sci-Fi Exposure Bundle which features 8 thr

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/02/27/marathon-reviewsofar-blogroll-1772235737503.jpg

Humble Bundle is celebrating its 15th anniversary with a new Sci-Fi Exposure bundle that features Bungie's Marathon , RoboCop: Rogue City , Ghostrunner , and 5 more games. For as low as $25, you can add all 8 of them (which you can see below) to your Steam library, which sure beats paying the usual total cost for all of them together at $375, if you ask me. It's only available for another 20 days, though, so the countdown has begun to add this stack of sci-fi games to your PC library.
Humble Bundle 15th Anniversary Sci-Fi Exposure Bundle
Games included:

If you want to pay more than $25 for this bundle, you can actually send a little extra cash to Humble, publishers, and a charity called charity: water, which is a non-profit that helps bring clean drinking water to people in developing countries. From Humble's main page for this bundle, you can also adjust your donation to choose how much money you want to send and to where, which is helpful so you can know where it's going.

On the other hand, paying less than $25 nets you fewer games from the bundle. So, if you decide to pay at least $15, you'll get six games from the lineup instead, which are Crysis 3 Remastered, Crysis 2 Remastered, Crysis Remastered, RoboCop: Rogue City - Collection, Ghostrunner 2, and Ghostrunner. If you drop below that to $10, you'll only get RoboCop: Rogue City - Collection, Ghostrunner 2, and Ghostrunner, so you're missing out on quite a few exciting games, including Marathon.

This game is certainly one of the standouts of this bundle. It's one we had a great time playing, with writer Travis Northup calling it "a ruthless and unforgiving extraction shooter that’s worth every ounce of hell it puts you through" in his 9/10 review.

Both Ghostrunner and Ghostrunner 2 earned high praise from us as well - scores of 8 and 9, respectively - and even RoboCop: Rogue City is a game we consider "the video game equivalent of a B movie in the best way," landing with a score of 7/10. So, no matter which game you jump into from this bundle's lineup, you're sure to have an excellent time booting it up on PC.

Humble has had quite a few great bundles popping up lately that are worth checking out alongside this one. Looking for a little something to play for Halloween? The Cozy After Dark Showcase Bundle is full of some delightfully spooky picks. There's also the Double Fine Publisher Bundle , which features some excellent titles like Psychonauts and Brutal Legend to play. And of course, the October Humble Choice is well worth a look while it's still live.

items.title: 暴雪表示，《魔兽世界》的《Forever》的分裂分层将在发布时得到重大改进
items.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever's layering system will receive some significant improvements for launch, according

content.v: World of Warcraft: Forever's layering system will receive some significant improvements for launch, according to a statement provided to GameSpot from Blizzard.

Layering, for the uninitiated, is a behind-the-scenes system in WoW: Forever that essentially creates and runs new versions (or layers) of the world as needed, all running simultaneously on top of one another. According to Blizzard, players in WoW: Forever are assigned a layer based on various criteria, like familiar players and friends, language, and PvP balance. Grouping up with a player or friend who is on another layer will transport you to the same layer so you can interact.

There are some pros to this system. It makes completing quests easier (since there's less competition for quests items and enemies) and the world far less crowded. It also helps performance, as anytime there are thousands of players in a concentrated area, like a capital city, the game can struggle to handle the load. Layering spreads those players out. It works wonders in modern WoW and has also been used to different degrees in various versions of WoW Classic in the past.

Unfortunately, there are also some huge downsides that have repeatedly surfaced over the course of the WoW: Forever beta. It doesn't take much searching on YouTube or Reddit to find countless instances of players complaining about layering. Leaving a group, crossing into a different zone, or traveling on a zeppelin or boat causes players to abruptly switch layers. The layering changes feel far more frequent and noticeable than in the past, ruining some of the charm that comes from having a persistent world filled with the same people.

Thankfully, changes are on the way. When asked if Blizzard would be making improvements to how it handles layering for launch and what players should expect, GameSpot received the following statement attributed to WoW: Forever associate production director Clay Stone:

"Bringing all players together within each ruleset, while also recreating some of the original WoW's 'small-realm-feel' social experiences such as repeat encounters with other recently met players in the game, is an important part of protecting and nurturing social experiences in WoW: Forever.

"However, as we've been playing the beta alongside players, we too have recognized areas where we need to make improvements, particularly when players may be unexpectedly separated from each other (both in terms of specific locations and in terms of frequency), and we absolutely are making improvements. Some examples of this are making sure players don't get decoupled from other players they see on transports (i.e. boats and zeppelins) after loading screens, as well as large groups of players getting layered when they enter or leave capital cities.

"Although there will always be some amount of layering that occurs within our high-capacity infrastructure, we're working on these improvements now ahead of launch, and players should expect that we'll consistently be making more improvements, as necessary, through launch and beyond, with the goal always being to make the world feel as seamless as possible."

That sounds like it will solve many of the instances players have complained about, including the scenario shown in a recent clip posted to the WoW Classic subreddit. It shows a group of players riding the boat from Kalimdor to Eastern Kingdoms, only to abruptly change layers. Suddenly, the entire boat is filled with hostile players from the opposing faction killing everyone on board. User Kippzo's post is simply titled "I can't believe the game is launching like this."

Another Reddit user highlighted how they went to join a large group of players dueling outside of a capital city, only to change layers when stepping outside to find a ghost town. Stone's statement specifically says Blizzard will make it so large groups of players will no longer change layers when exiting capital cities.

What Stone's statement doesn't address is layering when crossing zone boundaries, a case of particular concern to the game's player vs. player-community. Videos and clips shared online show large-scale world PvP battles evaporating into thin air as raids cross from one zone into another. Some even show players on a losing side of a battle intentionally running for the invisible border so they can phase into another layer and avoid death . Others are using layering to grief players guerilla-warfare style, killing unsuspecting foes and then fleeing to another layer before they can be retaliated against.

"I understand that there are technical limits making layering a necessary evil, but in its current iteration it just leads to an empty world for most players and an incredibly anti-fun experience," Reddit user RC_Rabbit said .

In a game where much of the appeal is the chance encounters, friendships, and rivalries made while out adventuring in the world, a system that divides players and can be exploited for nefarious purposes is a major problem. One Reddit user, Worried-Falcon-1973, said layering is a "glaring issue" that will "ruin" the game's open-world moments, and that the community needs to make more noise so that Blizzard understands how serious the matter is.

"We want to level in the world, sure, but then let us actually be able to stay with people of our layer and not shuffle us around wildly the moment I leave the city, the zone, the zeppelin, the tram, or whatever," they said.

Blizzard seems to be listening, though with Forever's beta now over and less than two weeks until launch, the community will have to wait for the full game to see how Blizzard's proposed improvements will shake out. WoW: Forever launches November 4. In other WoW: Forever news, Blizzard just announced a new server option for PvP-minded players.

items.title: 在粉丝抱怨他的脸后，即将推出的类似《质量效应》的《出埃及记》中的主角被粉丝抱怨了
items.summary: He's been looksmaxxing. He got the Chad surgery.

content.v: Archetype Entertainment has unveiled a new look for the protagonist of Exodus, its upcoming sci-fi RPG. We at PCG didn't love Jun Aslan's original face, but it sounds like there was more widespread discontent over his supposedly homely mug.

After a brief intro by studio GM Chad Robertson, we got a brief cinematic trailer of the new Jun⁠—with a little cameo by Matthew McConaughey, in case you forgot he's lending his voice to this game. And, I mean, yeah: Jun's a real prettyboy now. My man's looking like an industry plant. Cheekbones that could cut glass.

Previously, Jun was, perhaps, a little schlubbier, but only really by the standards of showbiz. I contend that he realistically could have been someone's workplace crush. He was an LA 6.5, but a Chicago 9. Prettier than most people you know, I'd wager. I didn't love Jun's original look, but I figured, hey, it's an RPG. I'll just mess with the sliders.

But it sounds like we're restricted to one face per sex in Exodus, based on the new trailer's description: "You can play Jun Aslan as male or female, and options like hairstyles, hair color, facial hair, and tattoos let you add your own personal touch." That sounds reminiscent of the facial presets from Baldur's Gate 3, but with only two characters instead of that game's two dozen or so.

I like making a cutie pie RPG character as much as the next guy, but now that he's gone, I find something endearing about the way Jun looked before he got his work done. You were beautiful just the way you were, honey. On a more meta level, I wish studios would double down when there's a backlash over minor aesthetic stuff: I don't even have a horse in the s&box race, but I prefer that game's original, controversial, sausage character model to the new realistic ones .

At the same time, as a clear attempt at a Mass Effect successor , Exodus has to live up to the generational good looks of Dutch Model Mark Vanderloo ⁠⁠—BioWare based the default male Commander Shepard face on him. Even with a full character creation suite, it's hard to justify a custom Shep who always winds up looking like a potato man when the real Handsome Squidward is right there for the taking.
What do you think? Should Jun have kept his original face, or does his new look suit him? Sound off in the comments (and we've got a poll after the newsletter block).

items.title: 实际上，使用动视“推荐”的 RTX 3060 Ti 显卡，《使命召唤：现代战争 4》运行得非常流畅，以下是我用来获得最佳性能的设置
items.summary: Though upscaling is somewhat of a requirement if you're at 1440p.

content.v: I've been having a grand old time playing Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 with an RX 9070 XT , but there'll be plenty of people wanting to run the game on older hardware. So, I decided to dust off my old and much-beloved workhorse, the RTX 3060 Ti , and see how it does in the new Activision shooter. I've been quite pleasantly surprised by the results.

Which is good news, considering Activision lists this graphics card, alongside the AMD RX 6600 XT and Intel Arc B580, as the 'recommended' ones to "run at 90 fps in multiplayer on High graphics settings."
I've found this actually pans out, provided you're at 1080p or are fine enabling Quality upscaling at 1440p.
RTX 3060 Ti performance in COD: MW4
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/YCfD5BENn8KFH9od8t5TdT-1920-80.jpg

As you can see from the chart below, at 1440p native, the game struggles to reach this 90 fps target even on the Minimum preset. And as I noted in my general performance overview —which, by the way, you should read if you want to know which specific settings to alter to improve your frame rate—the Balanced preset offers the best bang for your buck by far, as going up to Ultra lowers your frame rate significantly.
COD MW4 preset performance - 1440p - RTX 3060 Ti
Frame rates were taken at 1440p native, using an RTX 3060 Ti, Ryzen 7 7800X3D, and 32 GB of DDR5 RAM.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/bkwSqn4ocKYaQwBeFt2HHb.png

I captured these frame rates during the same repeated 30-second run in a campaign mission, but I've found they translate pretty well to DMZ, although a few frames are shaved off in that mode, and a few additional are shaved off when looking into the distance across the expansive map.
The trick to get buttery smooth frame rates with a GPU like the RTX 3060 Ti is to enable DLSS upscaling in Quality mode.

Enabling Quality upscaling takes frame rates from just above 60 to around 90 or even 100 when using the Balanced preset, if you opt for the older CNN model. I didn't notice much of a difference in visuals between CNN and Transformer models, so I'd be opting for the former just for the extra handful of frames, but either way you're getting something very playable.
DLSS Quality vs native at 1440p
This compares playing the game at 1440p native to the two different versions of DLSS upscaling, set to Quality.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/bkwSqn4ocKYaQwBeFt2HHb.png

All of the above is speaking to 1440p, but if you have a 1080p monitor or don't mind dropping to 1080p on your 1440p monitor, you can get some very nice frame rates from a card like the RTX 3060 Ti. As you can see from my final chart below, you can push about 130 fps on average in the campaign if you play at 1080p with DLSS enabled, again on the Balanced preset.
Comparing 1440p to 1080p performance
This chart compares performance at 1440p to 1080p using an RTX 3060 Ti, with upscaling enabled and disabled.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/bkwSqn4ocKYaQwBeFt2HHb.png

There are two caveats here, though. The first is that I wouldn't recommend doing this if you're on a 27-inch, 1440p monitor because it can look quite blurry. I'd just stick to 1440p with DLSS enabled instead.

The second caveat is that, in DMZ, I found frame rates to be a little lower than the ones I recorded in my runs of the campaign mission. But I'd still stick to those settings I just described. At 1440p with DLSS enabled in DMZ I get about 80–95 fps, and at 1080p with DLSS enabled I get about 110 fps.
The settings I'd use in COD: MW2 with an RTX 3060 Ti
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ADf8vRbBtWTiViXXLTEKWT-1920-80.jpg

This is the resolution and upscaling combo setup I'd personally use to actually play the game if I had a 27-inch, 1440p monitor: 1440p resolution, DLSS Quality upscaling (CNN), and the Balanced preset. If I was using a 24-inch, 1080p monitor, I'd stick to DLSS Quality (CNN) and the Balanced preset, but obviously have the resolution at 1080p instead. With a smaller 1080p monitor, it's not as blurry to have DLSS enabled even at 1080p.

The final bit of good news is that I've found my frame rate to be pretty consistent, too. With an RTX 3060 Ti, I get frame rates consistently pushing closer to 100 fps than 60 fps at 1440p with DLSS Quality enabled and using the Balanced preset.
Comparing higher to lower detail quality
High detail quality on the left, normal on the right. Notice the yellow/orange tree loses all detail in the right-hand image.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/xFCK2MB2Laec5Ca5WppqPM.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/dgtm3mxTXQVJhTGBoH9uPM.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/bkwSqn4ocKYaQwBeFt2HHb.png

A couple of final tips. One thing I'd recommend is avoiding the lower presets, and especially the bottom 'Minimum' one, as I found graphical fidelity takes a big hit when dropping that low. Everything is much more crisp at Balanced.

And finally: if you're okay sacrificing just a small handful of frames here and there, try turning your 'detail quality' setting up to High. I've found this eliminates some of the buggy, blocky trees and shrubbery you occasionally run into, and makes them look like actual trees.

items.title: AMD says the re-release of the Ryzen 7 5800X3D was 'like a final gift to our loyal [AM4] users' and it was CEO Dr. Lisa Su who first came up with the idea
items.summary: It timed itself rather nicely with the deepening memory crisis, too.

content.v: I was genuinely surprised by the re-release of the AMD Ryzen 7 5800X3D earlier this year. A chip I thought long dead was back in 10th Anniversary form, after a resurrection process AMD's David McAfee described as " very hard, actually " to our Dave at Computex 2026.

Now AMD's Travis Kirsch has spoken to Japanese outlet Tech+ about more of the thinking behind the re-release, and it seems the idea started at the very top. "Originally, several years ago, I believe Lisa [Su, AMD CEO] was one of the people who suggested reviving the Ryzen 7 5800X3D."

"It was like a final gift to our loyal users who had used our AM4 for almost 10 years, giving them one last chance to upgrade their PCs using DDR4 systems," Kirsch continues. "However, this required restarting the production lines, which took some time. In short, this was planned before the changes in the memory market occurred, and it was not considered as a solution to the DDR5 shortage."

That may be the case, but the timing still worked out pretty well for AMD. DDR5 prices had been surging since October 2025, while the chip's eventual release date of June 25, 2026 put it right in the middle of a difficult year for PC gamers. Many of whom may well have been looking to upgrade older, AM4 rigs without making the switch to the DDR5-only AM5 socket.
Kirsch was also asked about the current shipment ratio of AM4 to AM5 processors. "I cannot give you the exact ratio," he says. "But I can say that AM4, which supports DDR4, remains very strong."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Ciw4CgpXpB3b9boopazYVc-1920-80.jpg

"As you know, AM4 shipments were very stable until we started to see fluctuations in memory prices, while AM5, which supports DDR5, continued to grow," says Kirsch. "In terms of AM4, it continues to perform well. As for AM5, recently we have seen growth in models equipped with 3D V-Cache."
Well, you didn't expect actual figures, did you? And as for future platforms, Kirsch remains similarly cagey about any talk around the AM5 socket's eventual replacement:

"I cannot answer when AM6 will be released, or whether it will even be released at all. However, I would like to explain our strategy. Platform lifespan is paramount for end users. It is important to have the option to simply upgrade the processor three years after purchasing a platform.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/eZ5rjhyDc55sU9DLWhjKf9-1920-80.jpg

"We understand that constantly refreshing the platform is not good for our partners or end users," says Kirsch. "So, when that time comes in the future, we will introduce a new platform, but we don't know when that will be."

AMD's next-generation Zen 6-based CPUs will use the existing AM5 socket, and rumours suggest they'll be pushing clockspeeds to new heights later this year. And as for the chips after that? We're probably looking at 2029 or later. So, there's plenty of time for AM5 to stick around, and who knows—maybe it'll be just as long-lasting as AM4 in the end.

items.title: AMD says its working on FSR's frame pacing issues, but there's still conspicuously no mention of Multi Frame Generation

content.v: Whether you dismiss it as 'fake frames' or embrace the tech as a real game changer, frame generation has fast become a headlining act of this GPU generation. We've since discovered that not all frame gen (FG) tech is created equal, but AMD has promised to address a key criticism of its own FSR FG.

Earlier this week, AMD's Jack Huynh announced that FSR 4.1 would be shipping early to RX 6000 graphics cards , though that wasn't all. Huynh also announced that improvements to FSR's frame pacing were on the way, too .

Personally, I'm more familiar with Nvidia's approach to FG—especially after unlocking Multi Frame Gen on my RTX 4070 Super earlier this year. AMD's FSR has often been criticised for how it struggles with frame pacing in comparison. Ie, you may have lots of frames , but not every one of them is displayed for a consistent amount of time, making for gameplay that's a different flavour of choppy.

The issue can affect frames both traditionally rendered and generated, and it's been a stumbling block since at least FSR 3. For example, CD Projekt noted gamers may experience micro stutter back when Cyberpunk 2077 got official support for the tech in 2024. As recently as August this year, Hardware Unboxed's testing demonstrated that pacing is still an issue in games that support both FSR 3.1 and FSR 4 (via Videocardz ).

It's good to hear that AMD is focusing on this issue, but without a solid timeline or a list of hardware set to enjoy these frame pacing improvements, this week's announcement amounts to little more than, 'We know, and we're working on it!'

Also conspicuously absent was any mention of Multi Frame Generation on AMD GPUs. Currently, AMD's Frame Generation generates one intermediary frame, though third-party developers have managed to crank that far higher . We already know MFG is on the way for AMD hardware , the question is more 'how soon?'
Here's hoping AMD's officially supported frame pacing improvements for FSR arrive before an enterprising third-party can show them how it's done.
